---
name: tavily-entity
description: |
  Fill in a company, person, or organization for a CRM from the web, using Tavily, including a CSV of rows the user already has. Identifies the right entity when others share the name, then fills the fields from authoritative sources. Use when the user wants to enrich an account, a spreadsheet, or a pasted list of known names, or says "enrich", "CRM", or "who is". For discovering matches use tavily-list. For a deep comprehensive report use tavily-research.
allowed-tools: Bash(tvly *)
---

# Tavily entity

Resolve one entity and return a CRM record. The name is not the identity.
Confirm which entity it is, then fill the record from authoritative sources.
Every value comes from a page you read. An empty field stays empty.

Search and extract as `tavily-search` describes; load it only if it isn't
loaded yet. To discover new matches use `tavily-list`; for a deep report use
`tavily-research`.

## Identify the entity first

People and companies share names. A record that mixes two of them is worse
than an empty one. Isolate a single entity before you fill any field.

1. Take the type (company, person, or organization) and every identifier the
   user already gave: a domain, a city, an employer, a title, a product.
2. Search the name and look for other entities that use it. A common name, a
   name that is also a product or a place, or a person with a common name is a
   collision until you prove otherwise.
3. You have the right entity only when two identifiers agree. For a company,
   the name plus its own domain. For a person, the name plus an employer, a
   location, or a profile they control, and the organization on that profile
   has to match. One page that mentions the name is not identification.
4. If more than one entity still fits, stop and return the candidates. Do not
   pick the one with more results, and do not copy a field from one candidate
   onto another.
5. Put a stable identifier, the domain or the employer, into every later
   search, not the bare name.

## Read authoritative sources

Fill a field from the page that owns the fact. Extract that page. A snippet is
not enough for a number.

- The entity's own site, an official profile, and a filing or registry come
  first for facts the entity publishes: what it is, where it is, who leads it,
  what it sells. For a person, the employer's team page or a profile the person
  controls comes before a people-search site.
- A directory, a data broker, or a roundup is a lead to that page. Use it as
  the source of a field only when no authoritative page states the fact, and
  say so in the source note.
- When two authoritative pages disagree on a number, keep the more direct one
  and record the other in the source note. Do not average them.
- Include a published email or phone number only when a page shows it.

Extract the pages that own the fields you need in one call. Search for recent
news, with the domain or employer in the query, only when the user wants recent
signals or a full record.

## A CSV of known rows

When the user already has the entities, in a file or a pasted table, enrich
those rows. Do not go looking for new names.

1. Read the rows and count them. Use the fields they named. If they did not
   name fields, ask once, then use the same fields on every row.
2. Above 25 rows, tell them the count and the fields and wait for a go-ahead.
3. For each row, follow Identify the entity first and Read authoritative
   sources. A row you cannot isolate stays unresolved: blank new fields, a note
   on what collided, and no guessed values.
4. Write the original columns plus the new fields, a source for each new
   field, and a status of `filled` or `unresolved` to
   `{name}-enriched-{YYYY-MM-DD}.csv`. Use a CSV writer.

The CSV is the result. In the reply, give the number filled, the number
unresolved, and the path. Do not paste a record per row.

## Output

When the user asked specific questions, answer those in the reply, with a source
for each value, and skip the template. For a full record, use this:

```markdown
# {Name}

type: company | person | organization
identified by: {domain, employer, or other stable identifier}
as_of: {YYYY-MM-DD}

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| website | | |
| description | | |
| industry | | |
| headquarters | | |
| founded | | |
| employees | | |
| funding | | |
| revenue | | |
| linkedin | | |

## People
| Name | Title | Source |
|---|---|---|

## Recent signals
- {YYYY-MM-DD}: {fact} — {url}

## Unknown
- {field}: {what you tried}
```

For a person, the field rows are title, organization, location, and profile URL,
and People appears only when the user asked for related people. Drop a field
row that does not apply to this type. A field that applies and could not be
filled stays in the table with a blank value and a line under Unknown.
Description is one or two sentences grounded in the about page or profile.
Recent signals are at most five dated items: funding, a launch, a leadership
change, hiring. Omit a section that has no rows.

When you cannot pick one entity:

```markdown
# {Query}

| Name | Website | What separates it from the others |
|---|---|---|
```

name: tavily-list
description: |
  Build a deduplicated table of matches for a set, using Tavily. The table is what search returned, not every match that exists. Use when the user wants a list, all of something, or a table with duplicates removed. Confirm the columns and a cap before searching. For one CRM record, or a CSV of rows they already have, use tavily-entity. For a deep comprehensive report use tavily-research.
allowed-tools: Bash(tvly *)
---

# Tavily list

Return the matches you can verify for a set, one row each, with duplicates
merged. The table is the result. It is not every match that exists. Do not
collapse rows into a summary, and do not call the table complete.

Use `tavily-search` to search and read pages. If it isn't installed, run `npx skills add tavily-ai/skills --skill tavily-search` and read its SKILL.md before continuing. When you open many list pages, save the responses and filter them the way that skill describes, so the raw pages stay out of context.

## When this is the wrong skill

- The user wants one record filled in, or fields added to a CSV of rows they already have. Use `tavily-entity`. If it isn't installed, run `npx skills add tavily-ai/skills --skill tavily-entity` and read its SKILL.md before continuing.
- The user wants a deep comprehensive report. Use `tavily-research`. If it isn't installed, run `npx skills add tavily-ai/skills --skill tavily-research` and read its SKILL.md before continuing.

## Steps

1. Before any search, fix the inclusion rule in one sentence, the columns, and
   a cap. Columns always include name, website or profile, a one-line
   description, and the source URL, plus any the user named. If they did not
   name the extra columns or a cap, ask once and wait. If the set is unbounded
   ("every restaurant"), that question includes the boundary, such as a city
   or a category. A row gets in only when it matches the inclusion rule.
2. Search the set from several angles: the category, "list of" roundups,
   directories, and the names that appear on pages you have already opened. One
   query does not cover the set. Pull every name off a page that is itself a
   list.
3. Give each row an identity. For an organization, that is the website host
   with `www` removed. For a person, it is the profile URL, or the name plus
   the organization when there is no profile. For a product on a shared host,
   it is the canonical URL.
4. Merge rows that share an identity. Keep the fuller row and record the names
   you folded in. When a match has no website yet, search for it once before
   you finish. If it still has none, keep the row and leave the website blank.
5. Stop at the cap, or when two new angles in a row add no rows. Say which.
   Either stop means this pass is finished. Neither means the set is complete.
6. When the user wants more, search again and exclude every name and website
   already in the table. Append only new rows, then merge by identity again.
   Raise the cap by the number they asked for.

Use the same columns on every row. Leave a cell blank when no page states it.

Use `tavily-entity` for a row only when the user asked for CRM fields on each match. If it isn't installed, run `npx skills add tavily-ai/skills --skill tavily-entity` and read its SKILL.md before continuing. Otherwise a list row stays a list row.

## Output

Show the table in the reply, and save the same markdown to `lists/{title}.md`
in the working directory. The title is sentence case, 3 to 6 words, letters,
numbers, and single spaces.

```markdown
# {Title}

Inclusion: {one sentence}
As of: {YYYY-MM-DD}
Cap: {N}
Stop: {two angles added nothing | hit the cap}
Rows: {count after dedup}
Coverage: not exhaustive. This is what the angles below returned.

| Name | Website | Description | {asked columns} | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Merged
- {kept name} ← {other names} ({shared website})

## Coverage
Angles: {the queries and the list pages you opened}
Excluded this pass: {names and websites already kept, or none}
Likely gaps: {the part of the set this pass could not see}
```

name: tavily-monitor
description: |
  Build a Tavily search or extraction that runs on a cadence, with a saved baseline. Search monitors set max_age_hours to the interval so a cached copy from before it is not returned. Use when the user wants to monitor, track, watch, or be alerted when something changes, or asks for a recurring check of a query or a page. For a deep comprehensive report use tavily-research. For a one-time lookup use tavily-search. For a one-time table use tavily-list.
allowed-tools: Bash(tvly *)
---

# Tavily monitor

Turn a watch into a search or an extraction that can run again unchanged, then
run it once and save the baseline. The monitor file is the result.

Use `tavily-search` to run the check. If it isn't installed, run `npx skills add tavily-ai/skills --skill tavily-search` and read its SKILL.md before continuing.

## When this is the wrong skill

- The user wants a deep comprehensive report. Use `tavily-research`. If it isn't installed, run `npx skills add tavily-ai/skills --skill tavily-research` and read its SKILL.md before continuing.
- The user wants every current match, once. Use `tavily-list`. If it isn't installed, run `npx skills add tavily-ai/skills --skill tavily-list` and read its SKILL.md before continuing.

## Pick the kind

| You have | Kind | What "changed" means |
|---|---|---|
| A topic, and the pages are not known yet | search | A result URL that was not in the previous snapshot |
| One or more known URLs | extract | The hash of that page's extracted content changed |

Use search for mentions, news, jobs, and anything where new pages appear. Use
extract for a pricing page, a changelog, a docs page, or a status page.

## Steps

1. Write the query or the URL list so the next run can reuse it verbatim. Follow
   `tavily-search` for how to shape it. Leave dates and "latest" out of the
   query. The snapshot, not the wording, decides what is new.
2. Write the change rule in one sentence. For a search, a new URL is the
   alert. A URL from the last snapshot that is missing this run is not an
   alert: a page that could not be fetched live is left out. For an extract, a
   changed hash is the alert, and the alert quotes the part the user cares
   about (the price, the version), not the whole page.
3. Name a cadence. Use the one the user asked for. If they did not, use daily
   for news and changelogs, and weekly for a page that changes slowly, and say
   which you chose. On a search, set `max_age_hours` to that interval in hours,
   so a cached copy older than the cadence is not returned. Daily is 24, weekly
   is 168. Use `0` when the interval is under an hour, and `720` when it is
   longer than 30 days. Read how the parameter works in the search reference of
   `tavily-search`. Write the number in the monitor file and send it on every
   run, including the first. Extract does not take `max_age_hours`.
4. Run it once. If the results are the wrong kind of thing, fix the query or
   the URLs and run again before you save anything. If the search is refused
   with `434`, the run did not complete. Say so, and leave `snapshot.json` as
   it was.
5. Save the monitor and the snapshot. The next run reads the monitor, runs the
   same search or extract, reports only what the change rule flags, and
   replaces `snapshot.json`.

Create `monitors/{name}/` in the working directory. The name is sentence case,
3 to 6 words, letters, numbers, and single spaces. Quote it in shell commands.

Do not start a scheduler unless the user asks for one. When they do, and the
environment has a way to run on that cadence, point it at this folder.

A later change to the query or the URL list is a new monitor. It gets a new
folder and a new baseline. Editing them in place makes the next diff meaningless.

## Output

`monitors/{name}/monitor.md`:

```markdown
# {Name}

- Cadence: {daily | weekly on Monday | the schedule the user asked for}
- Kind: search | extract
- Query: {the query, for a search}
- URLs: {one per line, for an extract}
- max_age_hours: {the cadence in hours, search only}
- Alert when: {the change rule}
- Snapshot: snapshot.json

## Run again

Read this file. Use `tavily-search` to run the same search or extract. On a
search, pass `max_age_hours` from this file. Compare the result to
snapshot.json using the alert rule above. Report only the changes. Then
replace snapshot.json with this run. If the search is refused with `434`,
report that and keep the snapshot.
```

`monitors/{name}/snapshot.json`:

```json
{
  "ran_at": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "kind": "search",
  "query": "",
  "items": [{ "url": "", "title": "", "snippet": "" }]
}
```

For an extract, store `pages` instead of `items`: `url`, `sha256` of the
extracted content, and a short excerpt of the part being watched.

In the reply, give the cadence, `max_age_hours` for a search, the query or the
URLs, the alert rule, and the folder path, plus what the baseline already shows.

name: tavily-research
description: |
  Research a topic in depth with Tavily. Use this skill when a question needs many sources gathered and weighed together: analysing a market, policy, technology or trend, comparing options across several criteria, reviewing the literature, or any request to research, investigate or analyze something in depth. A single fact or answer to find, even one with many clues, is a tavily-search task. For one CRM record use tavily-entity, for a table of matches use tavily-list, and for a recurring check use tavily-monitor.
allowed-tools: Bash(tvly *)
---

# Tavily research

Use this when the answer has to be built from many sources. A single fact or
answer to find is a search: follow `tavily-search` instead.

Search and read pages as `tavily-search` describes. Load it only if it isn't
loaded yet.

## Steps

### 1. Ask only when the answer would change the research

Ask when a term has two meanings, the user assumed a place, or a name is two
different entities. Otherwise start.

### 2. Split the question

Split into subtopics that do not overlap and that together cover the question.
Carry the user's limits with every subtopic: dates, places, and what is out of
scope. Use 3 subtopics when you are unsure, 4 for a comparison with separate
criteria, 5 for separate entities, regions or domains, and more only for a
large set.

### 3. Research the subtopics together

**With subagents:** choose a title of 3 to 6 words, create
`research_notes/{title}/` and `reports/` in the working directory, and start
one general-purpose subagent per subtopic in the same turn. Give each the
subtopic, the key questions, the user's limits, the absolute path of its notes
file, and this first step: read `references/researcher.md` at its absolute path
next to this skill.

**On your own:** run each subtopic's searches in parallel, as `tavily-search`
describes, and extract the main sources for each. Keep the findings and their
URLs in your context. Don't write notes files.

### 4. Fill thin parts, then write

Before writing, run another round for any part of the question that would
leave its section thin.

### 5. Write and deliver the answer

Follow `references/report-writer.md`. On your own, write it once, as
your reply. Save it to `reports/{title}.md` only when the user asked for a
file, and then give the path after the report. With subagents, have one agent
write `reports/{title}.md` from the notes, then give the user the full report
in your reply, followed by its path.

If this conversation already produced a report on the subject, build on it:
research only what is new or needs checking again.

# Tavily

Tavily is a search API designed for LLMs, enabling AI applications to access real-time web data.

## Installation

**Python:**
```bash
pip install tavily-python
```

**JavaScript:**
```bash
npm install @tavily/core
```

See **[references/sdk.md](references/sdk.md)** for complete SDK reference.

## Client Initialization

```python
from tavily import TavilyClient

# Uses TAVILY_API_KEY env var (recommended)
client = TavilyClient()

#With project tracking (for usage organization)
client = TavilyClient(project_id="your-project-id")

# Async client for parallel queries
from tavily import AsyncTavilyClient
async_client = AsyncTavilyClient()
```

## Choosing the Right Method

**For custom agents/workflows:**

| Need | Method |
|------|--------|
| Web search results | `search()` |
| Content from specific URLs | `extract()` |
| Content from entire site | `crawl()` |
| URL discovery from site | `map()` |

**For out-of-the-box research:**

| Need | Method |
|------|--------|
| End-to-end research with AI synthesis | `research()` |

## Quick Reference

### search() - Web Search

```python
response = client.search(
    query="quantum computing breakthroughs",  # Keep under 400 chars
    max_results=10,
    search_depth="advanced"
)
print(response)
```
Key parameters: `query`, `max_results`, `search_depth` (ultra-fast/fast/basic/advanced), `include_domains`, `exclude_domains`, `time_range`

See **[references/search.md](references/search.md)** for complete search reference.

### extract() - URL Content Extraction

```python
# Simple one-step extraction
response = client.extract(
    urls=["https://docs.example.com"],
    extract_depth="advanced"
)
print(response)
```
Key parameters: `urls` (max 20), `extract_depth`, `query`, `chunks_per_source` (1-5)

See **[references/extract.md](references/extract.md)** for complete extract reference.

### crawl() - Site-Wide Extraction

```python
response = client.crawl(
    url="https://docs.example.com",
    instructions="Find API documentation pages",  # Semantic focus
    extract_depth="advanced"
)
print(response)
```
Key parameters: `url`, `max_depth`, `max_breadth`, `limit`, `instructions`, `chunks_per_source`, `select_paths`, `exclude_paths`

See **[references/crawl.md](references/crawl.md)** for complete crawl reference.

### map() - URL Discovery

```python
response = client.map(
    url="https://docs.example.com"
)
print(response)
```

### research() - AI-Powered Research

```python
import time

# For comprehensive multi-topic research
result = client.research(
    input="Analyze competitive landscape for X in SMB market",
    model="pro"  # or "mini" for focused queries, "auto" when unsure
)
request_id = result["request_id"]

# Poll until completed
response = client.get_research(request_id)
while response["status"] not in ["completed", "failed"]:
    time.sleep(10)
    response = client.get_research(request_id)

print(response["content"])  # The research report
```

Key parameters: `input`, `model` ("mini"/"pro"/"auto"), `stream`, `output_schema`, `citation_format`

See **[references/research.md](references/research.md)** for complete research reference.

name: tavily-search
description: |
  Use this skill whenever a task needs the web: searching for information, checking current facts or news, finding sources, reading a URL, finding a page on a site, or collecting many pages from a site. Use it for anything past your training data or anything the user wants verified online.
allowed-tools: Bash(tvly *)
---

# Tavily search

Use the `tavily_search`, `tavily_extract`, `tavily_map` and `tavily_crawl` tools if your tool list has them
(some clients add a prefix such as `mcp__tavily__`). Otherwise run `tvly <command>` directly; there's no
need to check for it first. If neither works, follow [setup](references/setup.md).

Parameters are named as in the API (`max_results`). The CLI spells them as flags (`--max-results`) with
comma-separated lists (`--include-domains sec.gov,reuters.com`). For exact parameters, read the tool schema,
run `tvly <command> --help`, or see the [API reference](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search).

| You have | You need | Use |
|---|---|---|
| A question or topic | Sources, facts or news | Search |
| URLs | Their content | Extract |
| A site, not the exact page | The right page's URL | [Map](references/map.md) |
| A site section | Many of its pages | [Crawl](references/crawl.md) |

## Search

**Use advanced search.** Set `search_depth` to `advanced` (`--depth advanced` in the CLI) for every search
unless the user needs a fast answer to a simple lookup. It reaches more sources and ranks the passages that match your query.

**Write queries for a search engine.** Use the names and terms you expect on the page, not the user's whole
request. Split a question with several parts into one focused search per part. For a long written report,
search each part separately and extract the main sources for each before you write.

**Follow your leads.** When a result names a likely answer, test it right away: search that name with the
other details you know, or extract its page. Keep a lead that fits most details until a source contradicts it; a detail you can't confirm doesn't rule it out. When a search misses,
search the details again in their own words before adding names or filters you guessed, and build lists of
candidates from results, not memory. When a detail keeps coming back empty, work out what it refers to, such as
the role, event or term, and search for that.

`tvly search` prints each result's title, full URL and the first 600 characters of its matching passages. Add
`-o .tavily/<name>.json` to also save every result whole, so you can go back to it instead of searching again.
`--max-chars 0` prints the passages whole. Read a promising page in full with `tvly extract <url>`.

**Batch independent searches.** Issue the searches for one step together in one turn, one call each: separate
`tavily_search` calls with MCP tools, or separate Bash calls with the CLI, each holding a single `tvly` command.
MCP calls run in parallel; Bash calls run one after another but still use one turn. Avoid `&`, `$(...)` and
loops, which make the client ask for permission. Put the query in single quotes:
`tvly search 'Rust 2024 edition release date' --depth advanced --max-results 10 -o .tavily/rust-2024.json`.

**Work from saved files.** Keep results in `.tavily/` in the current folder and read them with `head`, `grep` or
`python3`. `-o` creates the folder and keeps it out of git, so don't create it yourself. For example, to find a name or number in a long page:

```bash
tvly extract 'https://example.com/report' -o .tavily/report.json
python3 -c 'import json,re; t=json.load(open(".tavily/report.json"))["results"][0]["raw_content"]; [print(t[max(0,m.start()-200):m.end()+200], "\n---") for m in re.finditer("2019", t)]'
```

Read pages with `tvly extract`, not `curl` or `wget`.

**Ask for 10 results.** Set `max_results` to 10 (`--max-results 10`). **Narrow before you widen.** Filters help more than raising `max_results` further. Use `time_range` or dates for
recent events or a stated period. Use `include_domains` when the answer lives on an official or named site; it
is a hard filter, so search again without it if it doesn't find the page.

**Keep large results on disk.** When a result is long, such as raw page content or a crawl, save it under
`.tavily/` and read only the parts you need. An MCP result lands straight in your context, so keep those calls
small.

**Save copies with `-o`.** Saving results to files is a job for `tvly`: run the call with
`-o .tavily/<name>.json`, even if you searched with MCP tools. A file you write from an MCP result is your
retyping of it, not the original. Without `tvly`, work from the results in your context and don't copy them
into files. If the user asked for a saved copy, give them the URLs and queries, say an exact copy needs the
CLI, and write a retyped copy only if they ask for one.

**Read the results critically.** Count independent sources, not results. Treat a generated answer as a summary
to check, never as a source.

## Extract

Extract returns up to 20 URLs per call as markdown, including pages built with JavaScript.

- Extract only the few results worth reading. Snippets answer most facts.
- Extract full pages by default. Pass `query` (`--query`) only to isolate one fact on a long page; if the passages come
  back cut off near what you need, extract again without it.
- Rerun with `extract_depth` set to `advanced` (`--extract-depth advanced`) when a page is built with JavaScript, the content is in a table, or
  `basic` came back empty. Check `failed_results` every time and say which pages couldn't be read.

## When to stop

- Stop once two independent sources agree on a fact.
- Before you answer, close any gap your draft would mark unconfirmed or fill from memory: run one targeted
  search or reread the saved page.
- For releases, ownership, official figures and decisions by a named body, confirm on the official domain or
  repository. A secondary site or a generated answer is not enough.

## Hand off the job

When the user wants an in-depth report that needs many sources gathered and weighed, such as an analysis, a
comparison across several criteria or an in-depth investigation, use `tavily-research` instead of your own searches.
If it isn't installed, run `npx skills add tavily-ai/skills --skill tavily-research` and read its SKILL.md first. A
single fact or answer to find stays here.

# @tavily/opencode-plugin

OpenCode plugin for [Tavily](https://tavily.com) — gives your AI agent reliable web search, content extraction, crawling, URL discovery, and deep research with citations.

Supports OpenCode **v1.18.29+ (1.x)** and **v2** using OpenCode's [documented dual-version entrypoint](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/migrate-v1): v1 calls `server()`, and v2 calls `setup()`.

## Installation

Add the plugin to your `opencode.json`. The configuration key differs between versions.

### OpenCode v2

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@tavily/opencode-plugin"]
}
```

### OpenCode v1.18.29+

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["@tavily/opencode-plugin"]
}
```

OpenCode installs the package automatically on next launch

### Install the Tavily CLI

Then install the Tavily CLI globally (requires Node.js 20.1 or later):

```bash
npm install -g @tavily/cli
```

`pnpm add -g`, `yarn global add`, and `bun add -g` work the same way.

## Authentication

On first use, the agent will prompt you to authenticate. You can also set up in advance:

```bash
# Browser login (recommended)
tvly login
# Or set an API key
export TAVILY_API_KEY=tvly-your-api-key
```

Get an API key at [tavily.com](https://tavily.com).

If `TAVILY_API_KEY` is set in your environment, the plugin automatically passes it to shell commands.

## What It Does

This plugin registers the [Tavily Agent Skills](https://github.com/tavily-ai/skills) with OpenCode:

| Skill | Use it for |
|-------|------------|
| `tavily-search` | Web search, reading URLs, mapping and crawling sites with the `tvly` CLI |
| `tavily-research` | Multi-source research reports with citations |
| `tavily-entity` | Filling in a company or person record from the web |
| `tavily-list` | Building a deduplicated table of matches |
| `tavily-monitor` | Recurring checks for new information on a topic |
| `tavily-sdk` | Adding Tavily to application code with the Python or JavaScript SDK |

It also tells the agent to pass `--client-name opencode` to `tvly` commands for request attribution.

## Development

The plugin lives in the `.opencode-plugin/` folder of [tavily-ai/skills](https://github.com/tavily-ai/skills). `./build.sh` copies the repo's skills into the package, and `npm pack` runs it automatically. Publishing a release of the repo publishes the package to npm at the release version.

# Tavily in OpenCode

When you run `tvly search`, `tvly extract`, `tvly map`, `tvly crawl` or `tvly research`, add `--client-name opencode` after the subcommand, for example `tvly search "query" --json --client-name opencode`.

If `tvly` is missing or not signed in, follow the setup reference in the `tavily-search` skill.

# Writing the report

You turn the research notes into one report that answers the question. You do
not search or read new pages. A claim that is not in the notes, with a URL,
does not go in the report.

## Read first

Read every notes file in the folder you were given. When the assignment names
an earlier report and its notes, read those too. Where they disagree with the
new notes, the new notes win. The report has to stand on its own. The reader
is not sent back to the earlier file.

Paths may contain spaces. Quote them in shell commands.

## Shape

```markdown
# {Title: about six words, with a verb, stating the finding}

{One paragraph that answers the question, then the stakes and the context the reader needs. Someone who stops here should still know the answer.}

## {Signpost heading that states a specific finding}
{Prose. **Bold** the figures and names a reader would scan for. Cite a checkable claim as ([Source](URL)).}

## {Next finding}
{Same form.}

## Conclusion
{One or two paragraphs on what the findings imply. Nothing restated from above.}
```

Use one section for each part of the question, and give each named entity,
region or mechanism its own subsection with its figures.

## Headings

Sentence case. A reader who reads only the headings should get the argument.
Put the specific result in the heading.

| Writes the finding | Names the topic |
|---|---|
| Migratory geese forage 370 extra hours a year | Effects of climate on geese |
| Usage pricing costs more past 50 seats | Pricing |

## Prose

Use a table when several items share the same fields. Each section adds a step
in the argument.

Cite the claims a reader would want to check: figures, dates, and attributed
positions. Use `([Source](URL))` inline. Skip a finding whose note has no URL.

When the notes disagree, say so in the paragraph and say which source you take
and why. State what nobody confirmed. Take a position the evidence supports,
and say what is still open without filling it with "may" or "possibly".

The conclusion is the implication. It is not a summary of the sections.

# Researching one subtopic

You cover only the subtopic you were given. Other work is covering the rest.

Your notes are the only material the report writer gets. It will not search
again, so every finding the report might use has to be in the file, with its
URL.

## Before you search

Use `tavily-search` for every search and page read. If it isn't installed, run
`npx skills add tavily-ai/skills --skill tavily-search` and read its SKILL.md
before continuing. Follow that skill for how to write a query, when to extract
a page, and when to save large results and filter them. Do that before the
first search.

## How to gather

1. Name the gaps that stand between you and the key questions.
2. Search for those gaps. Run independent searches in parallel.
3. Extract the pages you expect to cite. A snippet is a lead. A number, a date,
   or a quote needs the page.
4. Repeat until a stop condition below is met.

Prefer the authoritative source, and cite that page. That is the institution
in a position to know: the company's own site, the paper, the filing, the
dataset, the official docs, a government or regulator, or a standards body.
Use another source when it adds a fact the authoritative page does not, and
say which is which.

When a page is long, or you are opening several at once, save the response and
filter it the way `tavily-search` describes, and write the notes from that
result. Keep the URL next to the fact.

Search again with different words when a query is thin. Repeating the same
query returns the same pages. For a recent topic, trust what you just
retrieved over your training data.

A subtopic usually takes about eight searches and extracts. Stop by twelve.

## When to stop

- The key questions have sourced answers.
- New searches return pages you already have.
- You are approaching twelve calls.

## What may go in the notes

Write a finding only when you can point at the page it came from. When several
pages support the same fact, cite the authoritative page. Cite a news story,
blog, or aggregator only when that page does not state the fact. When two
sources disagree, record both, authoritative first, and the disagreement.
When you cannot find a reliable source, write that as a gap. A gap is a useful
result.

Leave out a claim that is only a prediction, an unnamed source, or a number
that appears on aggregators and nowhere else, unless you label it that way in
the finding.

## Notes file

Save the file at the path in your assignment. The parent folder exists. Use
these sections, and no other top-level sections:

```markdown
# {Subtopic}

## {Key question}

### Takeaway
{One or two sentences.}

### Cited findings
- {Fact} — [Authoritative source](URL)
- {Fact only another source has} — [Secondary source](URL)
- {Fact} — [Authoritative source](URL); contradicted by [Other source](URL)

### Inferences
- {What the findings support, beyond what any one page states.}

### Gaps
- {What you could not answer, and what you tried.}
```

Repeat the key-question section for each question you were given. Every bullet
under Cited findings has a URL, and that URL is the authoritative page when
one exists. A fact with no URL goes under Gaps instead.

## Crawl vs Map

| Feature | Crawl | Map |
|---------|-------|-----|
| **Returns** | Full content | URLs only |
| **Speed** | Slower | Faster |
| **Best for** | RAG, deep analysis, documentation | Site structure discovery, URL collection |

**Use Crawl when:**
- Full content extraction needed
- Building RAG systems
- Processing paginated/nested content
- Integration with knowledge bases

**Use Map when:**
- Quick site structure discovery
- URL collection without content
- Planning before crawling
- Sitemap generation

## Instructions and Chunks

Use `instructions` and `chunks_per_source` for semantic focus and token optimization:

```python
response = client.crawl(
    url="https://docs.example.com",
    max_depth=2,
    instructions="Find all documentation about authentication and security",
    chunks_per_source=3  # Only top 3 relevant chunks per page
)
```

**Key benefits:**
- `instructions` guides crawler semantically, focusing on relevant content
- `chunks_per_source` returns only relevant snippets (max 500 chars each)
- Prevents context window explosion in agentic use cases
- Chunks appear in `raw_content` as: `<chunk 1> [...] <chunk 2> [...] <chunk 3>`

**Note:** `chunks_per_source` only works when `instructions` is provided.

## Path and Domain Filtering

### Path patterns (regex)

```python
# Target specific sections
response = client.crawl(
    url="https://example.com",
    select_paths=["/docs/.*", "/api/.*", "/guides/.*"],
    exclude_paths=["/blog/.*", "/changelog/.*", "/private/.*"]
)

# Paginated content
response = client.crawl(
    url="https://example.com/blog",
    max_depth=2,
    select_paths=["/blog/.*", "/blog/page/.*"],
    exclude_paths=["/blog/tag/.*"]
)
```

### Domain control (regex)

```python
# Stay within subdomain
response = client.crawl(
    url="https://docs.example.com",
    select_domains=["^docs.example.com$"],
    max_depth=2
)

# Exclude specific domains
response = client.crawl(
    url="https://example.com",
    exclude_domains=["^ads.example.com$", "^tracking.example.com$"]
)
```

## Map then Extract Pattern

Consider using Map before Crawl/Extract to plan your strategy:

1. **Use Map** to get site structure
2. **Analyze** paths and patterns
3. **Configure** Crawl or Extract with discovered paths
4. **Execute** focused extraction

```python
# Step 1: Map to discover structure
map_result = client.map(
    url="https://docs.example.com",
    max_depth=2,
    instructions="Find all API docs and guides"
)

# Step 2: Filter discovered URLs
api_docs = [url for url in map_result["results"] if "/api/" in url]
guides = [url for url in map_result["results"] if "/guides/" in url]
print(f"Found {len(api_docs)} API docs, {len(guides)} guides")

# Step 3: Extract from filtered URLs
target_urls = api_docs + guides
response = client.extract(
    urls=target_urls[:20],  # Max 20 per extract call
    extract_depth="advanced",
    query="API endpoints and usage examples",
    chunks_per_source=3
)
```

**Benefits:**
- Discover site structure before committing to full crawl
- Identify relevant path patterns
- Avoid unnecessary extraction
- More control over what gets extracted

## Performance Optimization

### Depth vs Performance

Each depth level increases crawl time exponentially:

| Depth | Typical Pages | Time |
|-------|---------------|------|
| 1 | 10-50 | Seconds |
| 2 | 50-500 | Minutes |
| 3 | 500-5000 | Many minutes |

**Best practices:**
- Start with `max_depth=1` and increase only if needed
- Use `max_breadth` to control horizontal expansion
- Set appropriate `limit` to prevent excessive crawling
- Process results incrementally rather than waiting for full crawl

### Rate Limiting

- Respect site's robots.txt
- Monitor API usage and limits
- Use appropriate error handling for rate limits
- Consider delays between large crawl operations

### Conservative vs Comprehensive

```python
# Conservative (start here)
response = client.crawl(
    url="https://example.com",
    max_depth=1,
    max_breadth=20,
    limit=20
)

# Comprehensive (use carefully)
response = client.crawl(
    url="https://example.com",
    max_depth=3,
    max_breadth=100,
    limit=500
)
```

## Common Pitfalls

| Problem | Impact | Solution |
|---------|--------|----------|
| Excessive depth (`max_depth=4+`) | Exponential time, unnecessary pages | Start with 1-2, increase if needed |
| Unfocused crawling | Wasted resources, irrelevant content, context explosion | Use `instructions` to focus semantically |
| Missing limits | Runaway crawls, unexpected costs | Always set reasonable `limit` value |
| Ignoring `failed_results` | Incomplete data, missed content | Monitor and adjust parameters |
| Full content without chunks | Context window explosion | Use `instructions` + `chunks_per_source` |

## Extraction Approaches

### Search with include_raw_content

Get search results and content in one call:

```python
response = client.search(
    query="AI healthcare applications",
    include_raw_content=True,
    max_results=10
)
```

**When to use:**
- Quick prototyping
- Simple queries where search results are likely relevant
- Single API call convenience

### Direct Extract API (Recommended)

Two-step pattern for more control:

```python
# Step 1: Search
search_results = client.search(
    query="Python async best practices",
    max_results=10
)

# Step 2: Filter by relevance score
relevant_urls = [
    r["url"] for r in search_results["results"]
    if r["score"] > 0.5
]

# Step 3: Extract with targeting
extracted = client.extract(
    urls=relevant_urls[:20],
    query="async patterns and concurrency",  # Reranks chunks
    chunks_per_source=3  # Prevents context explosion
)

for item in extracted["results"]:
    print(f"URL: {item['url']}")
    print(f"Content: {item['raw_content'][:500]}...")
```

**When to use:**
- You want control over which URLs to extract
- You need to filter/curate URLs before extraction
- You want targeted extraction with query and chunks_per_source

## Query and Chunks

Use `query` and `chunks_per_source` to get only relevant content and prevent context window explosion:

```python
extracted = client.extract(
    urls=[
        "https://example.com/ml-healthcare",
        "https://example.com/ai-diagnostics",
        "https://example.com/medical-ai"
    ],
    query="AI diagnostic tools accuracy",
    chunks_per_source=2  # 2 most relevant chunks per URL

```

**When to use query:**
- To extract only relevant portions of long documents
- When you need focused content instead of full page extraction
- For targeted information retrieval from specific URLs

**Key benefits of chunks_per_source:**
- Returns only relevant snippets (max 500 chars each) instead of full page
- Chunks appear in `raw_content` as: `<chunk 1> [...] <chunk 2> [...] <chunk 3>`
- Prevents context window from exploding in agentic use cases

**Note:** `chunks_per_source` only works when `query` is provided.

## Extract Depth

| Depth | When to use |
|-------|-------------|
| `basic` (default) | Simple text extraction, faster |
| `advanced` | Dynamic/JS-rendered pages, tables, structured data, embedded media |

```python
# For complex pages
extracted = client.extract(
    urls=["https://example.com/complex-page"],
    extract_depth="advanced"

```

**Fallback strategy:** If `basic` fails, retry with `advanced`:

```python
result = client.extract(urls=[url], extract_depth="basic")
if url in [f["url"] for f in result.get("failed_results", [])]:
    result = client.extract(urls=[url], extract_depth="advanced")
```

**Timeout tuning:** If latency isn't critical, set `timeout=60.0` for better success on slow pages.

## Advanced Filtering Strategies

Beyond query-based filtering, consider these approaches before extraction:

| Strategy | When to use |
|----------|-------------|
| Score-based | Filter search results by relevance score |
| Domain-based | Filter by trusted domains |
| Re-ranking | Use dedicated re-ranking models for precision |
| LLM-based | Let an LLM assess relevance before extraction |
| Clustering | Group similar documents, extract from clusters |

### Optimal Workflow

1. **Search** to discover relevant URLs
2. **Filter** by relevance score, domain, or content snippet
3. **Re-rank** if needed using specialized models
4. **Extract** from top-ranked sources with query and chunks_per_source
5. **Validate** extracted content quality
6. **Process** for your AI application

### Example: Complete Pipeline

```python
import asyncio
from tavily import AsyncTavilyClient

client = AsyncTavilyClient()

async def content_pipeline(topic):
    # 1. Search with sub-queries for breadth
    queries = [
        f"{topic} overview",
        f"{topic} best practices",
        f"{topic} recent developments"
    ]
    responses = await asyncio.gather(
        *(client.search(q, search_depth="advanced", max_results=10) for q in queries)
    )

    # 2. Filter and aggregate by score
    urls = []
    for response in responses:
        urls.extend([
            r['url'] for r in response['results']
            if r['score'] > 0.5
        ])

    # 3. Deduplicate
    urls = list(set(urls))[:20]

    # 4. Extract with error handling
    extracted = await asyncio.gather(
        *(client.extract(urls=[url], query=topic, extract_depth="advanced")
          for url in urls),
        return_exceptions=True
    )

    # 5. Filter successful extractions
    return [e for e in extracted if not isinstance(e, Exception)]

asyncio.run(content_pipeline("machine learning in healthcare"))
```

**Each failed_results object:**

## Summary

1. **Use query and chunks_per_source** for targeted, focused extraction
2. **Choose Extract API** when you need control over which URLs to extract from

4. **Choose appropriate extract_depth** based on content complexity

6. **Implement error handling** to manage failed extractions gracefully

```python
def tavily_search(**kwargs):
    return tavily_client.search(**kwargs)

def process_tool_call(name, args):

        return tavily_search(**args)
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown tool: {name}")
```

#### Main chat function

```python
def chat_with_claude(user_message: str):
    # Call 1: allow tool use
    initial_response = client.messages.create(
        model=MODEL_NAME,
        max_tokens=4096,
        system=SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": user_message}]}],
        tools=tools,
    )

    # If Claude answers without tools, return text directly
    if initial_response.stop_reason != "tool_use":
        return "".join(
            block.text for block in initial_response.content
            if getattr(block, "type", None) == "text"
        )

    # Execute all requested tools
    tool_result_blocks = []
    for block in initial_response.content:
        if getattr(block, "type", None) == "tool_use":
            result = process_tool_call(block.name, block.input)
            tool_result_blocks.append(
                {
                    "type": "tool_result",
                    "tool_use_id": block.id,
                    "content": json.dumps(result),
                }
            )

    # Call 2: send tool results and ask Claude for final synthesis
    final_response = client.messages.create(
        model=MODEL_NAME,
        max_tokens=4096,
        system=SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        messages=[
            {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": user_message}]},
            {"role": "assistant", "content": initial_response.content},
            {"role": "user", "content": tool_result_blocks},
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [{
                    "type": "text",
                    "text": "Please synthesize the final answer now based on the tool results above. Include 3-7 bullets and a Sources section with URLs.",
                }],
            },
        ],
    )

    return "".join(
        block.text for block in final_response.content
        if getattr(block, "type", None) == "text"
    )
```

## Overview

The Research API conducts comprehensive research on any topic with automatic source gathering, analysis, and response generation with citations. It's an end-to-end solution when you need AI-powered research without building your own pipeline.

---

## Prompting Best Practices

Define a **clear goal** with all **details** and **direction**.

**Guidelines:**
- **Be specific when you can.** Include known details: target market, competitors, geography, constraints
- **Stay open-ended only for discovery.** Make it explicit: "tell me about the most impactful AI innovations in healthcare in 2025"
- **Avoid contradictions.** Don't include conflicting constraints or goals
- **Share what's already known.** Include prior assumptions so research doesn't repeat existing knowledge
- **Keep prompts clean and directed.** Clear task + essential context + desired output format

### Example Queries

**Company research:**
```
Research the company ____ and its 2026 outlook. Provide a brief overview
of the company, its products, services, and market position.
```

**Competitive analysis:**
```
Conduct a competitive analysis of ____ in 2026. Identify their main
competitors, compare market positioning, and analyze key differentiators.
```

**With prior context:**
```
We're evaluating Notion as a potential partner. We already know they
primarily serve SMB and mid-market teams, expanded their AI features
significantly in 2025, and most often compete with Confluence and ClickUp.
Research Notion's 2026 outlook, including market position, growth risks,
and where a partnership could be most valuable. Include citations.
```

## Basic Usage

Research tasks are two-step: initiate with `research()`, retrieve with `get_research()`.

```python
import time
from tavily import TavilyClient

client = TavilyClient()

# Step 1: Start research task
result = client.research(
    input="Latest developments in quantum computing and their practical applications",
    model="pro"
)
request_id = result["request_id"]

# Step 2: Poll until completed
response = client.get_research(request_id)
while response["status"] not in ["completed", "failed"]:
    print(f"Status: {response['status']}... polling again in 10 seconds")
    time.sleep(10)
    response = client.get_research(request_id)

# Step 3: Handle result
if response["status"] == "failed":
    raise RuntimeError(f"Research failed: {response.get('error', 'Unknown error')}")

report = response["content"]
sources = response["sources"]
```

## Streaming vs Polling

**Streaming** — Best for user interfaces where you want real-time updates.
**Polling** — Best for background processes where you check status periodically.

### Streaming

Enable real-time progress monitoring with `stream=True`.

```python
stream = client.research(
    input="Latest developments in quantum computing",
    model="pro",
    stream=True
)

for chunk in stream:
    print(chunk.decode('utf-8'))
```

### Event Types

| Event Type | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| **Tool Call** | Agent initiates action (Planning, WebSearch, etc.) |
| **Tool Response** | Results after tool execution with sources |
| **Content** | Research report streamed as markdown (or JSON with `output_schema`) |
| **Sources** | Complete list of sources, emitted after content |
| **Done** | Signals completion |

### Tool Types

| Tool | Description | Models |
|------|-------------|--------|
| `Planning` | Initializes research strategy | mini, pro |
| `WebSearch` | Executes web searches | mini, pro |
| `Generating` | Creates final report | mini, pro |
| `ResearchSubtopic` | Deep research on subtopics | pro only |

### Typical Flow

1. `Planning` tool_call → tool_response
2. `WebSearch` tool_call → tool_response (with sources)
3. `ResearchSubtopic` cycles (Pro mode only)
4. `Generating` tool_call → tool_response
5. `Content` chunks (markdown or structured JSON)
6. `Sources` event
7. `Done` event

See [streaming cookbook](https://github.com/tavily-ai/tavily-cookbook/blob/main/cookbooks/research/streaming.ipynb) and [polling cookbook](https://github.com/tavily-ai/tavily-cookbook/blob/main/cookbooks/research/polling.ipynb) for complete examples.

```python
                "growth_rate": {"type": "number", "description": "Annual growth percentage"}
            }
        }
    },
    "required": ["summary", "key_points"]
}

result = client.research(
    input="Electric vehicle market analysis 2024",
    output_schema=schema
)
```

### Schema Best Practices

- **Write clear field descriptions.** 1-3 sentences explaining what the field should contain
- **Match the structure you need.** Use arrays, objects, enums appropriately (e.g., `competitors: string[]`, not `"A, B, C"`)
- **Avoid duplicate fields.** Keep each field unique and specific
- **Use `required` arrays** to enforce mandatory fields at any nesting level

**Supported types:** `object`, `string`, `integer`, `number`, `array`

### Streaming with Structured Output

When `output_schema` is provided, content arrives as structured JSON:

```python
stream = client.research(
    input="AI agent frameworks comparison",
    model="mini",
    stream=True,
    output_schema={
        "properties": {
            "summary": {"type": "string", "description": "Executive summary"},
            "key_points": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
        },
        "required": ["summary", "key_points"]
    }
)

for chunk in stream:
    data = chunk.decode('utf-8')
    print(data)  # Content chunks will be structured JSON
```

## Query Optimization

**Keep queries under 400 characters.** Think search query, not long-form prompt.

**Break complex queries into sub-queries:**
```python
# Instead of one massive query, break it down:
queries = [
    "Competitors of company ABC",
    "Financial performance of company ABC",
    "Recent developments of company ABC"
]
responses = await asyncio.gather(*(client.search(q) for q in queries))
```

## Search Depth

Controls the latency vs. relevance tradeoff:

| Depth | Latency | Relevance | Content Type |
|-------|---------|-----------|--------------|
| `ultra-fast` | Lowest | Lower | Content (NLP summary) |
| `fast` | Low | Good | Chunks |
| `basic` | Medium | High | Content (NLP summary) |
| `advanced` | Higher | Highest | Chunks |

**Content types:**
- **Content**: NLP-based summary of the page, providing general context
- **Chunks**: Short snippets (max 500 chars) reranked by relevance to your query

**When to use each:** 
- `ultra-fast`: Latency-critical (real-time chat, autocomplete)
- `fast`: Need chunks but latency matters
- `basic`: General-purpose, balanced relevance and latency
- `advanced`: Specific information queries, precision matters - default (Still fast and suitable for almost all use cases) 

## Key Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `query` | string | Required | Search query (keep under 400 chars) |
| `search_depth` | enum | `"basic"` | `"ultra-fast"`, `"fast"`, `"basic"`, `"advanced"` |

# Using crawl well

Crawl starts from a URL, follows links, and returns the content of each page
it reaches. Use it when you need many pages from one site, such as a whole
docs section, a changelog archive, or pages that aren't linked from the main
navigation.

## Always focus the crawl

An unfocused crawl returns every page it reaches and fills your context with
content you won't use. Give every crawl `instructions` that describe the
content you want. When the results go into your context, also ask for chunks
per page (`chunks_per_source`, where your channel supports it) so each page
comes back as its relevant parts instead of in full.

## Start small

Each extra level of depth multiplies the number of pages and the time the
crawl takes. Start at depth 1 with a `limit` of about 20 pages, look at what
came back, and widen the crawl only if the pages you need are missing. Always
set a `limit`, because without one a crawl can run much longer and cost much
more than expected.

## Aim it at the right section

When you know the section you need, restrict the crawl to it with
`select_paths`, such as `/docs/.*`, instead of starting at the home page. When
you don't know the site, map it first and build the path patterns from the
URLs you see.

## Reading pages or saving them

There are two reasons to crawl. When you need the content to answer a
question, keep the crawl focused and chunked as described above. When the user
wants a copy of the site, such as docs to keep locally, they want full pages
saved as files. Only the CLI can write files directly (`--output-dir`); tell an
MCP user that saving files needs the CLI.

## Check what failed

Look at `failed_results` after every crawl. Retry pages that failed with
`advanced` extract depth, and tell the user about any section the crawl
couldn't read.

Full parameter list: https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/crawl

# Using map well

Map lists the URLs on a site without reading their content, so it is much
faster than crawling. Use it when you know which site holds the answer but not
which page, or when you need to see how a site is organized before you crawl
it.

## Find a page, then extract it

The most common use is a two-step lookup. Map the site with `instructions`
that describe what you're looking for, such as "API authentication" or
"pricing and plans", then extract the one or two URLs that match. This costs
much less than crawling the site to find a single page.

## Learn the structure before a crawl

When you need many pages from a site you don't know, map it first and read the
paths. The URL patterns tell you which section to crawl, for example
`/docs/api/` instead of the whole domain, and they let you write `select_paths`
patterns that match real URLs.

## Keep it bounded

Map starts one level deep from the URL you give it. Raise the depth only when
the page you need is buried, and keep a `limit` on every call. If the site has
a docs or blog subdomain, start the map there instead of at the home page.

Full parameter list: https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/map

# Setup

Tavily is available as an MCP server or as the `tvly` CLI. Use whichever one
the agent already has. Set up the other only when the user asks, or when the
task needs something only that channel offers. Saving crawled pages as files, and saving a large search or extract so you
can filter it, both need the CLI.

## MCP

The remote server is at `https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp`. Clients that support
OAuth can connect to that URL and sign in through the browser. Other clients
pass an API key, either in the URL as `?tavilyApiKey=<key>` or as an
`Authorization: Bearer <key>` header.

In Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http tavily https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp
```

In Codex, add the server and then sign in through the browser:

```bash
codex mcp add tavily --url https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp/
codex mcp login tavily
```

For other clients, see the setup steps in the
[tavily-mcp README](https://github.com/tavily-ai/tavily-mcp). Adding a server
usually takes effect after the client restarts, so tell the user that a restart
may be needed instead of retrying the tool right away.

If an MCP call fails with an authentication error, ask the user to reconnect
the server or check their API key. Don't try to work around it from inside the
session.

## CLI

Install it if `tvly` is missing. It needs Node.js 20.1 or later:

```bash
npm install -g @tavily/cli
```

Use `pnpm add -g`, `yarn global add`, or `bun add -g` when that is the
package manager on the machine. If none of them is available, tell the user
that the CLI needs Node.js and use MCP instead.

Search and extract work without an account, up to a keyless rate limit. Don't
look for an API key or sign in before the first search or extract. Map, crawl
and research need authentication.

For first-time agent setup, start keyless unless the user asks to sign in or
the task needs map, crawl or research:

```bash
tvly init --skip-auth
```

When authentication is needed, run guided setup with `tvly init`, or `tvly init
--no-browser` to print the sign-in link instead of opening it. `tvly init`
reuses an existing credential, installs or updates the Tavily skills, and runs
a live test search. Use `tvly init --skip-skills` when the skills are already
installed. To sign in without the rest of setup, use `tvly login` or set
`TAVILY_API_KEY`. To save a key the user gave you, pipe it in with
`tvly login --api-key -` instead of passing it as an argument, which would put
it in shell history. Don't run `tvly login --api-key` with no value yourself:
without a terminal it waits for the key on stdin.

The browser sign-in returns to a localhost callback on the machine that runs
`tvly`. In a remote session, that callback must be reachable, which may need
SSH port forwarding. In an unattended agent or CI job, don't start a sign-in
flow. Leave authentication to the user or use a `TAVILY_API_KEY` they provided.

### Keyless limit

If search or extract hits the keyless limit in an interactive session, run
`tvly login`, then retry the original command once. In an unattended session,
report the limit and the ways to authenticate instead. Don't start a second
login right after guided setup finished.

### CLI details

- Quote every URL, because the shell treats `?` and `&` as special characters.
- Check the current login with `tvly --status --json` only when something
  fails. Don't run it before every command.
- Keep the CLI current with `tvly update --check` and `tvly update`.
- Run `tvly <command> --help` for the full list of options.
- Exit codes: 0 means success, 1 a setup or update failure, 2 bad input, 3 an
  authentication error, and 4 an API or live-test error.
